evidence.why: Placement, null-spawn branch, decrement, and terminal reset.
Chain ownership guard and cleanup writes.

facts.rationale: Replaces guaranteed per-stock spawning with the actual fallible creation path and preserves the ordered cross-file data flow.
facts.value: Forwards the fighter object unchanged first to ftSk_SpecialN_80111FBC and then to ftSk_SpecialS_CheckAndDestroyChain. With a non-null held-needle reference, the first callee clears that reference and repeatedly attempts thrown-needle creation while stored stock is nonzero, using ground/air-specific vertical placement; each iteration decrements stock even if creation returns null. It always finally resets stock to zero. The Chain callee guards on its owned pointer, requests destruction, invokes guarded working-state handling, then clears Chain ownership and both damage/death callbacks.

evidence.why: Nested callback identity test and both callback clears.
Separate Chain guards, numeric state write, and terminal clears.

facts.rationale: Restores the omitted outer held-object guard and preserves the separate Chain helper guard without assigning an unsupported meaning to state 2.
facts.value: Always invokes needle cleanup before Chain cleanup. Needle discharge attempts and callback-identity testing occur only when the held-needle reference was non-null. Inside that branch, either death2_cb or take_dmg_cb matching this wrapper causes both callbacks to be cleared; without a held reference, needle cleanup only resets stock. Chain cleanup is a no-op without an owned Chain; otherwise it requests destruction, invokes ChainSomething (whose own non-null guard controls its article call and numeric working-state write of 2), and clears Chain ownership and both interruption callbacks.
